root.statement: Ω has a cause of its own, in another dimension that this graph cannot measure or determine and that may require an entirely different logic. Ω is the root of the graph, not an uncaused arising; its substrate requirement points beyond the graph.

principles.statement: Level 0 is an abstraction. It shows arising under the poorest rules: in something homogeneous and fully uniform, something arises that is no longer homogeneous with the original, and this first inhomogeneity makes all further arising possible. If all complexity formed by itself, the basic rule is extremely simple: something arises through the interaction of something, and such arisings form a complex system.

domains.name: Admissibility lineage
domains.definition: The Level-0 abstraction of the basic rule, from the homogeneous proto-field Ω through distinction, resonant closure and ensembles to the quantum seed, together with the Level-1 cells hypothesized directly from it.
domains.criteria: A formal Level-0 construct (methodological placeholder) that abstracts arising under the poorest conditions, or a higher-level arising whose arising causes are Level-0 cells without an established physical mechanism (metacausation hypothesis, as 1.32-1.34). Meta-structural arisings of Level 13 would join here.

domains.name: Fields, particles and physical matter
domains.definition: Quantum fields, the particle families and their interactions, the vacuum, and their direct physical consequences in nuclei, atoms and electromagnetic regimes of matter.
domains.criteria: What arises is a quantum-field structure, particle family, interaction, symmetry-breaking or vacuum regime, or a nuclear, atomic, electromagnetic or optical regime of matter described without chemical bonding or biological function. Nuclear effects measured in chemical or biochemical surroundings stay here (2.17, 2.18). Gravitational and cosmic arisings (Level 12) would join here.

domains.name: Molecular organization and cell machinery
domains.definition: Chemical bonding, intermolecular forces and condensed phases, the biomolecular systems they make possible (templates, nucleic acids, proteins, metabolism, membranes, protocells, viruses), and the internal machinery of the cell.
domains.criteria: What arises is a bond type, intermolecular force, phase or interface; a biomolecular structure, reaction network, template process or molecular quality-control system; a membrane, compartment or protocell; or the cell's internal organization (organelles, trafficking, cytoskeleton, metabolism, electrochemical state). Signalling, gene regulation and fate decisions of cells, and responses that defend a cell against damage, belong to the next two domains.

domains.name: Signalling, development and organismal coordination
domains.definition: Cellular signalling, gene regulation and cell-fate control, and the multicellular form and organ-level coordination they build: morphogenesis, tissues and organs, vasculature, nervous and endocrine coordination, and sensory organs.
domains.criteria: What arises is a signalling or gene-regulatory regime of cells, a cell-fate process (division, death, differentiation, contact), or a structure or coordination system of the multicellular body formed through them (tissue pattern, organ, vasculature, nervous or endocrine system, sensory periphery).

domains.name: Homeostasis, defence and repair
domains.definition: Processes that keep a cell, tissue or organism within viable bounds and restore it after perturbation: stress and damage responses, senescence, immunity and inflammation with their chronic regimes, organ homeostasis, repair and regeneration, and their neural regulation.
domains.criteria: What arises maintains or restores the integrity of a cell, tissue or organism against perturbation or threat: stress, genome-maintenance, autophagy and senescence responses; innate or adaptive immunity; inflammation, its resolution and chronic regimes; organ homeostasis and trophic regulation; repair, regeneration and adult stem-cell niches; or neural control of these (neuro-immune, neurovascular, psychosomatic).

domains.name: Behaviour, cognition and society
domains.definition: Organization carried by the neural networks of behaving organisms (circuits, brain dynamics, perception, action, affect, cognition) and by interacting agents (sociality, exchange, norms, institutions, culture, information environments).
domains.criteria: What arises is organized by neural networks as the basis of behaviour (formation and plasticity of circuits, brain rhythms and states, perception and action, affect, cognition, consciousness, symbolic representation) or by interacting agents and their shared structures (roles, exchange, collective decisions, norms, institutions, culture, information environments). Neural regulation of immunity and body state belongs to homeostasis-defence. Technological and civilizational arisings (Levels 8 and 10) would join here unless they show a lineage of their own.

clusters.name: First distinctions and oscillatory admissibility
clusters.definition: The root proto-field Ω, the first distinction with its two primitive directions and the compensation they require, the indefinite frame, the variational functional with its closure parameter and discrete scale, the admissible oscillatory modes it selects, and frame-stable selection among them.

clusters.name: Resonant closure and the localized CRT node
clusters.definition: Triadic resonant closure, its configurational density, its persistence under small admissible deformation and its nonlinear self-binding, which together make the localized CRT node admissible.

clusters.name: Ensembles and the quantum seed
clusters.definition: Coupled CRT-node ensembles with their coupling functional and synchronization mode, the ensemble-scale quantum seed, and the bridge to the effective Level-1 field.

clusters.name: Directional branch of the localized node
clusters.definition: The anisotropy, directional deformation, directional admissibility gradient and transport bias of the formed node, which lead to the Level-1 anisotropy hypotheses.

clusters.name: Level-0 anisotropy hypotheses
clusters.definition: Hypothesized and speculative Level-1 anisotropies whose arising causes are the Level-0 gradient and transport-bias cells rather than an established field mechanism.

clusters.name: Quantum field framework
clusters.definition: The architecture and dynamics of quantum fields, their differentiation into gauge and matter sectors, renormalization-group structure and entanglement.

clusters.name: Vacuum structure and fluctuations
clusters.definition: The structured ground state of quantum fields, its fluctuations and virtual excitations, and their effects on particle properties and on primordial cosmological perturbations.

clusters.name: Strong interaction
clusters.definition: Quarks and gluons, the running of the strong coupling, asymptotic freedom, nonperturbative gauge-field organization, flux-tube structure and the confinement of color.

clusters.name: Hadronic and nuclear matter
clusters.definition: Color-neutral composites formed under confinement: hadronization, hadron families, protons and neutrons with their electromagnetic structure, atomic nuclei, and the influence of quark-level structure on matter.

clusters.name: Electroweak sector, Higgs and leptons
clusters.definition: Leptons, photons, W and Z bosons, electroweak symmetry breaking, the Higgs vacuum, mechanism, boson and mass generation, neutrino mass and oscillation, and particle decays.

clusters.name: Nuclei, atoms and nuclear-electronic coupling
clusters.definition: Primordial light nuclei, bound atomic structure and the periodicity of the elements from shell filling, and nuclear transitions coupled to their electronic or solid surroundings (hyperfine structure, Mössbauer effect, environment-sensitive decay channels).

clusters.name: Electromagnetic regime and optics of matter
clusters.definition: The electromagnetic interaction as the organizing regime of matter and its macroscopic consequences: Casimir forces and the reflection, scattering and propagation of light in media.

clusters.name: Chemical bonding, delocalization and reactions
clusters.definition: Covalent, ionic and metallic bonding, resonance and π-conjugation, chemical reactions over activation barriers, and quantum effects in chemical reactions.

clusters.name: Intermolecular forces and liquids
clusters.definition: Polarization and dipole interactions, van der Waals forces and hydrogen bonds, the self-organization of liquids they produce, and the hydrophobic effect of water.

clusters.name: Condensed phases and interfaces
clusters.definition: Crystalline and quasicrystalline order, thermodynamic phase regimes and transitions, colloids and interfacial boundaries, and the piezo- and ferroelectric properties of crystals.

clusters.name: Prebiotic monomers and template chemistry
clusters.definition: Activated monomers, complementary pairing rules and non-enzymatic template-directed polymerization: the Differentiation phase of Level 3.

clusters.name: Nucleic-acid replication, expression and chromatin
clusters.definition: Replication and transcription, the genetic code and translation, RNA folding and ribozymes, non-coding RNA and RNA interference, and chromatin packaging and modification.

clusters.name: Viral assembly and infection
clusters.definition: Capsid self-assembly, virion maturation, genome organization, receptor attachment and infection, and viral reprogramming of the host's expression apparatus.

clusters.name: Protein folding, catalysis and allostery
clusters.definition: Folding into functional conformations, active sites and enzymatic catalysis, cooperativity and enzyme complexes, allosteric regulation, and protein-structured hydration and ionic microenvironments.

clusters.name: Protein quality control and modification
clusters.definition: Chaperone-assisted folding, post-translational modification and selective proteasomal degradation.

clusters.name: Metabolic networks and bioenergetics
clusters.definition: Collectively autocatalytic networks, metabolic cycles and their compartmentalization, reaction kinetics and thermodynamics, ATP generation, pump-sustained electrochemical gradients, and redox, pH and ionic balance.

clusters.name: Membranes, compartments and protocells
clusters.definition: Ion channels and transport structures, enzymatic lipid synthesis and bilayer self-assembly, condensates, and protocellular permeability, encapsulation, growth-division cycles, chemiosmosis and selection.

clusters.name: Molecular recognition and signal transduction
clusters.definition: Antigen-antibody recognition, signal-transduction architectures and photopigment photochemistry: the molecular sensing steps on which cellular signalling, vision and immunity build.

clusters.name: Cell organization and organelles
clusters.definition: Prokaryotic cell organization, eukaryotic compartmentalization and the endosymbiotic origin of organelles.

clusters.name: Membrane trafficking, cytoskeleton and cell motility
clusters.definition: Endocytosis and exocytosis, the secretory pathway and protein sorting, cytoskeletal transport, intracellular spatial organization, and whole-cell motility.

clusters.name: Cellular metabolism and electrochemical state
clusters.definition: Integrated cellular energy metabolism, cell-state control of metabolic flux, and the membrane potential with its electrochemical gradients.

clusters.name: Cell signalling, gene regulation and sensing
clusters.definition: Cellular signalling and communication, gene expression control, integrated regulatory networks, environmental sensing and the phototransduction cascade.

clusters.name: Cell division, cycle control, death, differentiation and contact
clusters.definition: Cell division and its cycle control, apoptotic cell death, differentiation into specialized states, and stable intercellular contacts that prepare multicellularity.

clusters.name: Stress responses, genome maintenance, autophagy and senescence
clusters.definition: Cellular homeostasis and stress response, DNA repair, autophagy and its nutrient-sensing control, cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype.

clusters.name: Cellular immunity and inflammatory signalling
clusters.definition: Cellular immune responses, innate pattern recognition, inflammasome and cytokine signalling, macrophage polarization, T-cell exhaustion, NK surveillance and trained innate memory.

clusters.name: Morphogenesis, organogenesis and tissue architecture
clusters.definition: Tissue pattern formation, organogenesis, structural integration, basic tissue types, the extracellular matrix and its influence on cell phenotype, and the development of the vascular network.

clusters.name: Neural, endocrine and vasomotor coordination
clusters.definition: The nervous and endocrine systems as organ-level coordination architectures, their neuroendocrine integration, the vasomotor regulation of tissue perfusion, and their control of gene expression and proliferation in target tissues.

clusters.name: Eye and retinal processing
clusters.definition: The eye's optical interface, retinal sampling geometry, retinal circuit preprocessing and ganglion-cell spike encoding.

clusters.name: Repair, regeneration and stem-cell niches
clusters.definition: Tissue repair and regeneration, niche-regulated stem cells, and adaptive or pathological tissue reconfiguration.

clusters.name: Organ homeostasis and trophic regulation
clusters.definition: Organ-scale physiological regulation and the trophic constraint of cellular metabolism by tissue and organ conditions.

clusters.name: Tissue, barrier and metabolic inflammation
clusters.definition: Inflammatory tissue microenvironments, gut-barrier failure and endotoxemia, adipose immune remodeling and the inflammation-metabolism feedback loop.

clusters.name: Immune defence architecture and inflammaging regimes
clusters.definition: The organism-scale defence architecture, its resilience and allocation trade-offs, resolution capacity across its efficient and failing range, chronic low-grade inflammation, inflammaging hysteresis and age-associated immune remodeling.

clusters.name: Circuit formation, plasticity and activity-dependent gene regulation
clusters.definition: Formation of neural networks, synaptic plasticity, activity-dependent epigenetic and transcriptional change, restricted adult neurogenesis and structural remodeling of mature circuits.

clusters.name: Glial regulation of neural circuits
clusters.definition: Regulation of neural activity and circuit structure by astrocytes, microglia and myelinating oligodendrocytes.

clusters.name: Brain rhythms, neuromodulation and global states
clusters.definition: Oscillations, global neurotransmitter modulation, neuronal avalanches and near-critical network dynamics, and sleep-wake regulation.

clusters.name: Cognition, consciousness and symbolic representation
clusters.definition: Cognitive processing and decisions, functional specialization and connectome information processing, working memory and executive functions, conscious experience and symbolic representation.

clusters.name: Affect and social cognition
clusters.definition: Emotional and affective processing and the neural mechanisms of social recognition and empathy.

clusters.name: Perception, vision and motor control
clusters.definition: Sensory integration and perception, the thalamocortical visual pathway with its top-down modulation, and motor coordination.

clusters.name: Neural regulation of immunity and body state
clusters.definition: Neuro-immune interaction, neurovascular coupling and placebo or psychosomatic modulation of physiology.

clusters.name: Animal sociality, roles and practices
clusters.definition: Social organization of animals, roles and stratification, recurrent social practices and insect superorganisms.

clusters.name: Exchange, collective decision and markets
clusters.definition: Social exchange and resource coordination, collective decision-making, collective intelligence and market dynamics.

clusters.name: Societal structures, governance and institutions
clusters.definition: Structures of human society, political governance, complex institutions, cities, large-scale cooperation and conflict, and supranational governance.

clusters.name: Norms, identity and cultural evolution
clusters.definition: Social norms, social identity, cultural and linguistic evolution, cultural transmission, the hybridization of traditions, and the feedback through which social environments shape individual neural regimes.

clusters.name: Networked information environments
clusters.definition: Digital social and influence networks, epistemic markets, shared information environments, opinion polarization and mass cognitive distortion regimes.

arisings.Name: Field Distinguishability
arisings.ShortDescription: Minimal admissible pattern of sustained difference arising within the proto-field of admissibility, enabling comparison and subsequent differentiation.
arisings.Description: Field Distinguishability is the first admissible structural pattern of repeatable difference arising within the Proto-field of Admissibility. It introduces the minimal condition under which one region, state, or excitation can be structurally distinguished from another without presupposing metric space, temporal flow, or fully developed physical operators. The arising does not denote a material object, localized carrier, or completed effect. It denotes a reproducible ontological pattern of difference-preservation that makes comparison possible and thereby opens the admissible basis for later temporal distinction, spatial distinction, compensation relations, and localization structures. Within SOMA this arising functions as a methodological foundational pattern rather than an empirically isolated physical entity.

arisings.Name: Temporal Distinction
arisings.ShortDescription: System-level property of directed sequential differentiation, enabling ordered variation within the admissible field.
arisings.Description: Temporal Distinction denotes the admissible property by which distinguishable configurations can be ordered along a directed sequence. It does not presuppose physical time, measurable duration, or a metric continuum. Instead, it expresses the minimal ordered differentiability required for successive states to be structurally compared as earlier and later within the pre-metric Proto-field of Admissibility as already rendered distinguishable by Field Distinguishability. Within SOMA this arising is treated as a property rather than a process, because it characterizes the field as possessing an axis of ordered variation rather than constituting a completed transformation in itself. Temporal Distinction provides the ontological basis for directed change, later dynamical description, and the admissibility of compensatory and action-like structures at Level 0.

arisings.Name: Spatial Distinction
arisings.ShortDescription: System-level property of directional contrast across admissible variation, enabling localization within the field.
arisings.Description: Spatial Distinction denotes the admissible property by which distinguishable configurations can be differentiated across an abstract axis of separation. It does not presuppose physical space, metric extension, or geometric coordinates. Instead, it expresses the minimal structural condition under which contrast can be localized and compared as separation within the pre-metric Proto-field of Admissibility as already rendered distinguishable by Field Distinguishability. Within SOMA this arising is treated as a property rather than a process, because it characterizes the field as possessing an axis of localization rather than constituting a completed transformation in itself. Spatial Distinction provides the ontological basis for gradients, positional differentiation, and later configurational stabilization at Level 0.

arisings.Name: Compensation Energy
arisings.ShortDescription: System-level scalar property expressing the compensatory cost required to stabilize admissible distortions within the field.
arisings.Description: Compensation Energy denotes the admissible scalar property by which the already differentiated admissibility field registers the structural cost of sustaining and stabilizing directed distortions. It does not yet denote physical energy as a conserved substance, measurable thermodynamic quantity, or fully dynamical variable. Instead, it functions as a compensatory property that aggregates admissible deviation into a unified scalar measure of structural tension. Given temporal distinction and spatial distinction, this arising binds ordered variation and localized contrast into a common compensatory frame, making it possible to evaluate stabilization demand, compare admissible configurations, and prepare later variational selection. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because it characterizes the field through a derived scalar attribute rather than constituting an object, process, or completed effect.

arisings.Name: Admissible Wave Coherence
arisings.ShortDescription: Dynamically persistent coherence regime in which oscillatory variation remains structurally stable under Level-0 admissibility constraints.
arisings.Description: Admissible Wave Coherence denotes the admissible process by which oscillatory variation remains structurally persistent under ordered temporal distinction, localized spatial distinction, and compensatory scalar tension. Its stability is not only continuous but also becomes compatible with discrete compensatory selection, allowing repeatable bounded modes rather than arbitrarily diffuse oscillatory support. It is not yet a physical wave in the empirical field-theoretic sense and does not presuppose experimentally established wave equations. Instead, it marks the first dynamically sustained coherence regime within the Level-0 admissibility framework, where recognizable oscillatory form can persist through variation without collapsing into undifferentiated fluctuation. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity lies in ongoing coherent variation rather than in a bounded object or a static property. This arising provides the formal dynamical carrier required for later resonance closure, localization criteria, and node-like persistence.

arisings.Name: Admissibility Variational Functional
arisings.ShortDescription: Structural pattern of a variational admissibility functional that filters permissible Level-0 configurations.
arisings.Description: Admissibility Variational Functional denotes the structural pattern by which temporal distinction, spatial distinction, and compensation energy are integrated into a single variational admissibility form whose stationary configurations are the admissible oscillatory modes. This functional is written within the Minimal Geometric Admissibility Frame, so that admissibility selection is not purely algebraic but geometrically bounded, and its scalar closure term separates bounded oscillatory organization from scale-free propagation. It is not a physical Lagrangian in the established field-theoretic sense and does not claim empirical law status. Instead, it acts as a formal filtering rule that distinguishes admissible from inadmissible Level-0 configurations by organizing how variation, gradient structure, and compensatory cost can coherently combine. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a reproducible structural rule of filtering rather than a specific object, ongoing process, or derived property. This arising provides the filter through which admissible wave coherence is selected and the formal backbone for later resonance conditions, localization mechanisms, and configurational closure at Level 0.

arisings.Name: Triadic Resonant Closure (CRT Condition)
arisings.ShortDescription: Structural pattern of triadic resonant closure forming the first nontrivial coherent contour within Level-0 admissibility.
arisings.Description: Triadic Resonant Closure (CRT Condition) denotes the structural pattern by which three admissibly coherent oscillatory modes enter a closed resonant relation. This arising is not a directly asserted physical interaction law and not a single empirical event. It is the formal triadic closure condition under which three modes mutually reinforce and constrain one another such that the contour cannot be reduced to independent pairwise relations. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a reproducible structural condition of closure rather than a localized object or a scalar property. The CRT condition establishes the first nontrivial coherent contour at Level 0 and provides the formal basis for later configurational density, resonant localization, and node formation.

arisings.Name: Configurational Density
arisings.ShortDescription: Invariant scalar property measuring the localization and coherence of a closed resonant configuration.
arisings.Description: Configurational Density measures the concentration of a closure regime that has become sufficiently integrable to sustain localized admissibility rather than merely transient coherent overlap. It is not a physical mass density, probability density, thermodynamic density, or material concentration. This concentration is grounded in a closure regime whose compensatory support is discretely stabilizable rather than indefinitely continuous. Instead, it functions as an invariant configurational measure that aggregates the resonance structure into a single descriptor of how concentrated and coherent the contour has become under admissible transformation. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because it characterizes the state of a resonant configuration rather than constituting a new object or an independent dynamic process. Configurational Density provides the first proto-localization criterion at Level 0 and prepares the transition from closed resonant contour to node-like persistence.

arisings.Name: Resonant Localized Configuration (CRT-Node)
arisings.ShortDescription: Persistent localized configuration formed by closed triadic resonance and stabilized by internal feedback and configurational concentration.
arisings.Description: Resonant Localized Configuration (CRT-Node) denotes the admissible object-like formation obtained when a closed triadic resonant contour achieves sufficient configurational concentration and internal feedback stability to persist as a localized unit. It is the first object-like unit at Level 0 with bounded identity, local support, and internal coherence. The CRT-node is not a classical particle and not an empirically asserted microscopic constituent of nature. It is a persistent resonant configuration whose stability depends on the closed coupling of constituent modes and the maintained concentration of the underlying configuration. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an object because it can be referenced as a stable localized unit that remains identifiable under small perturbations and can participate as a carrier in subsequent nonlinear interaction, ensemble formation, and higher-order closure.

arisings.Name: Nonlinear CRT Variational Functional
arisings.ShortDescription: Structural pattern of a nonlinear variational functional whose resonant coupling binds a closed triad into a self-sustaining localized node.
arisings.Description: Nonlinear CRT Variational Functional denotes the structural pattern by which the general admissibility variational functional is extended with a resonant coupling of the three modes of a closed triad, capturing the nonlinear closure through which a resonant localized configuration can form. It is not a physical interaction law and not an empirically fixed field equation. Instead, it is a formal variational pattern expressing how the constituent resonant modes are coupled so that localization, bounded amplitude, and internal reinforcement become admissible and remain stable under perturbation. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it defines a reproducible structural rule for nonlinear resonant stabilization rather than constituting an object, a scalar property, or a time-extended process in itself. This arising marks the transition from passive resonant closure to actively stabilized node coherence and prepares the basis for node-node interaction and ensemble-scale organization at Level 0.

arisings.Name: CRT-Node Ensemble
arisings.ShortDescription: Coordinated object composed of multiple interacting resonant localized nodes within a shared admissibility architecture.
arisings.Description: CRT-Node Ensemble denotes the admissible object-like formation obtained when multiple resonant localized configurations become organized into a coordinated multi-node arrangement within a shared admissibility architecture. It is not a mere aggregate of independent CRT-nodes. It is a structured ensemble whose members remain distinguishable while participating in stable relations of mutual influence, compatibility, and collective organization. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an object because the ensemble can be referenced as a persistent higher-order unit with identifiable internal composition and bounded organizational coherence. The ensemble establishes the first collective object at Level 0: it becomes admissible only through the bounded inter-node coupling expressed by the ensemble-level variational structure, and it provides the carrier basis for synchronization modes, ensemble-scale quanta, and higher-order configurational dynamics.

arisings.Name: Ensemble-Level Variational Functional
arisings.ShortDescription: Structural pattern of a higher-order variational functional whose bounded coupling of CRT-nodes makes a coordinated ensemble admissible.
arisings.Description: Ensemble-Level Variational Functional denotes the structural pattern by which the local functionals of multiple resonant localized configurations and their bounded inter-node couplings are integrated into a single higher-order admissibility form. It is not a physical law and not a standalone dynamical process. Instead, it expresses the ensemble-level rule by which cross-node coupling, compatibility constraints, compensatory redistribution, and collective phase organization are structurally coordinated, so that the stability of a family of nodes no longer reduces to the sum of their separate persistences. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it defines a reproducible higher-order organizational form rather than a bounded object or derived scalar property. This arising establishes the variational architecture through which a coordinated node ensemble becomes admissible, together with its synchronization modes and the later emergence of ensemble-scale quanta at Level 0.

arisings.Name: Ensemble Synchronization Mode
arisings.ShortDescription: Collective property of phase-coordinated coherence across a CRT-node ensemble within a shared admissibility regime.
arisings.Description: Ensemble Synchronization Mode denotes the collective property by which a node ensemble can be characterized in terms of coordinated phase alignment, coherence, and variance reduction across its constituent resonant localized nodes. It does not describe the dynamics of any single node in isolation. Instead, it functions as an ensemble-level order property that expresses the degree to which the multi-node configuration behaves as a coordinated whole under shared admissibility conditions. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because it characterizes the ensemble through a derived collective descriptor rather than constituting a new object or a distinct variational pattern. This arising marks the transition from mere multi-node coexistence to an explicitly ordered collective regime and prepares the basis for ensemble-level quanta and effective coarse-grained descriptions at Level 0.

arisings.Name: Ensemble-Scale Quantum Seed
arisings.ShortDescription: Object-like ensemble-scale discrete unit emerging from coordinated CRT-node dynamics and preparing the transition to Level 1 field organization.
arisings.Description: Ensemble-Scale Quantum Seed denotes the admissible object-like unit formed when coordinated ensemble-level dynamics become sufficiently discrete and stable to function as the immediate precursor of Level-1 field organization. It is not yet a standard-model quantum object and does not claim direct empirical identity with known particles or field quanta. Instead, it marks the final Level-0 transition point at which collective admissibility architecture acquires a stable discrete carrier role capable of enabling the emergence of effective first-level field structure. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an object because it functions as a bounded ensemble-scale unit with persistent identity in the Level-0 to Level-1 transition.

arisings.Name: Bridge to Effective First-Level Field
arisings.ShortDescription: Effect-level bridge condition in which ensemble-scale discrete organization becomes admissible as the precursor of Level-1 effective field structure.
arisings.Description: Bridge to Effective First-Level Field denotes the admissible effect by which ensemble-scale discrete organization becomes sufficient to support the transition into Level-1 effective field structure. It is not itself the empirically established quantum-field domain and should not be read as already identical to Level-1 quantum fields. Instead, it functions as the bridging effect through which Level-0 admissibility architecture produces a coarse-grained precursor compatible with subsequent quantized field organization. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an effect because it expresses the produced transition outcome of ensemble-level closure rather than a stable Level-0 object or a reusable structural pattern. This arising marks the terminal bridge from methodological reconstruction to the first scientifically established field-theoretic level.

arisings.Name: Proto-field of Admissibility
arisings.ShortDescription: Foundational pattern of homogeneous admissibility within which distinguishable differences, ordering, and later Level-0 structures can arise.
arisings.Description: Proto-field of Admissibility denotes the foundational homogeneous pattern within which any later Level-0 distinction, compensation, coherence, and localization can become admissible. It is not a physical vacuum, material medium, metric space, or already formed field in the established scientific sense. Instead, it functions as the minimal ontological condition of structural admissibility: a pre-differentiated patterned foundation capable of sustaining later distinguishable variation without yet containing explicit temporal order, spatial separation, localized carriers, or stabilized physical operators. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern rather than an object or property because it does not designate a bounded carrier or a derived attribute, but the repeatable foundational form of homogeneous admissibility itself. This arising should be treated as the explicit predecessor of Field Distinguishability and as the deepest declared Level-0 foundation for subsequent methodological reconstruction.

arisings.Name: Minimal Geometric Admissibility Frame
arisings.ShortDescription: Minimal geometric property that permits stable ordered differentiation, bounded propagation, and invariant admissibility relations in Level-0 structures.
arisings.Description: Minimal Geometric Admissibility Frame denotes the minimal geometric property by which the two primitive directions of distinguishability and their compensatory balance become jointly admissible within one indefinite frame, sustaining ordered differentiation, bounded propagation, and invariant structural comparison. It is not yet a physical spacetime metric, coordinate manifold, or empirical geometry in the established scientific sense. Within SOMA it functions as the earliest admissible geometric condition under which temporal distinction, spatial distinction, compensation balance, and later wave coherence can become mutually consistent rather than remaining unconstrained variation; a definite frame would make the two directions equivalent and admit only same-sign accumulation of their contributions. This arising is classified as a property because it does not designate a separate carrier or an independent process, but the geometric admissibility condition of the already differentiated directions. It provides the minimal frame in which directional relations, interval-like ordering, the variational functional, and later variational stability become structurally meaningful at Level 0.

arisings.Name: Discrete Compensation Scale
arisings.ShortDescription: Minimal discreteness property by which compensatory balance becomes stably selectable as repeatable quanta of admissible variation.
arisings.Description: Discrete Compensation Scale denotes the minimal discreteness property by which compensatory balance becomes stably selectable as repeatable quanta of admissible variation rather than remaining fully continuous and indefinitely divisible. It is not yet a measured physical constant, numerical unit system, or already formalized quantum law in the established scientific sense. Within SOMA it functions as the earliest admissible scale-property that allows ordered distinction, compensatory cost, and bounded oscillatory support to be stabilized in discrete selectable portions. This arising is classified as a property because it does not designate an independent carrier or a separate process, but the scale condition under which compensation can recur in structurally stable units. In the Level-0 reconstruction this property later supports quantized relations between frequency-like, wave-like, and energy-like expressions, while still remaining an ontological admissibility condition rather than a completed physical formalism.

arisings.Name: Configurational Mass as Integrability Condition
arisings.ShortDescription: Integrability property by which bounded coherent configurations acquire stable resistance to dispersion and persistent localized admissibility.
arisings.Description: Configurational Mass as Integrability Condition denotes the property by which a bounded coherent configuration acquires stable resistance to dispersion and persistent localized admissibility. It is not yet a material substance, intrinsic particle stuff, or already completed physical mass concept in the established scientific sense. Within SOMA it functions as the earliest admissible property expressing that closure, compensation, and bounded coherence have become sufficiently integrated to sustain a persistent localized regime rather than a merely propagating or transient oscillatory one. This arising is classified as a property because it does not designate a separate carrier or a distinct process, but the integrability condition of an already formed coherent configuration. In the Level-0 reconstruction it marks the transition from bounded oscillatory support toward stable localized persistence, and later supports relations between closure, configurational density, node formation, and inertia-like admissibility effects.

arisings.Name: Frame-Stable Admissibility Selection
arisings.ShortDescription: Property by which admissibility selection remains stable under frame-conditioned variation and supports repeatable bounded configuration filtering.
arisings.Description: Frame-Stable Admissibility Selection denotes the property by which admissibility selection remains stable under frame-conditioned variation and can repeatedly filter bounded configurations without collapsing into unconstrained or frame-incompatible fluctuation. It is not a separate variational functional, geometric domain, or already completed physical law in the established scientific sense. Within SOMA it functions as the property through which the generic admissibility functional F[psi] becomes stably applicable inside the Minimal Geometric Admissibility Frame, so that coherent configurations are not merely evaluated abstractly, but selected in a way that preserves boundedness, repeatability, and compatibility with the foundational frame conditions of Level 0. This arising is classified as a property because it expresses a stabilized condition of selection rather than an independent carrier, object, or process. In the Level-0 reconstruction it strengthens the transition from generic admissibility filtering toward closure-capable and later localization-capable coherent support.

arisings.Name: Configurational Anisotropy
arisings.ShortDescription: Property by which a closed configuration exhibits directionally non-uniform organization of bounded support and localized admissibility.
arisings.Description: Configurational Anisotropy denotes the property by which a closed configuration exhibits directionally non-uniform organization of bounded support and localized admissibility rather than only scalar concentration. It is not yet a deformation process, external force, or completed physical field asymmetry in the established scientific sense. Within SOMA it functions as the earliest admissible property expressing that closure, density, and integrability can be organized directionally, so that support is distributed with structurally meaningful orientation instead of remaining isotropically concentrated. This arising is classified as a property because it does not designate an independent object or process, but the directional condition of an already formed coherent and localized configuration. In the Level-0 reconstruction it provides the first explicit bridge from scalar configurational concentration toward directed admissibility structure, and later supports directional configurational deformation, directional admissibility gradients, and localized transport bias.

arisings.Name: Closure-Preserving Deformation
arisings.ShortDescription: Process by which a closed resonant configuration undergoes small admissible deformations while retaining closure, bounded support, and integrable coherence.
arisings.Description: Closure-Preserving Deformation denotes the process by which a closed resonant configuration undergoes small admissible deformations without losing phase closure, bounded support, or integrable coherence. It is not yet arbitrary distortion, destructive perturbation, or externally imposed force response in the established scientific sense. Within SOMA it functions as the perturbative-persistence condition of object status at Level 0: a configuration that survives such deformation is a structurally stable unit rather than a fine-tuned singularity, and only together with bounded support and nontrivial configurational density does it qualify as the first object-like carrier. This arising is classified as a process because it expresses admissible change of a closed configuration under perturbation rather than a static property or independent object. In the Level-0 reconstruction it provides the persistence condition of the CRT-node and the capacity that directional deformation of the formed node presupposes.

arisings.Name: Directional Admissibility Gradient
arisings.ShortDescription: Property by which admissibility becomes directionally biased, yielding preferred orientation in the stability and transition landscape of a configuration.
arisings.Description: Directional Admissibility Gradient denotes the property by which admissibility becomes directionally biased, yielding a preferred orientation in the stability and transition landscape of a configuration. It is not yet a force field, imposed external vector, or completed physical potential gradient in the established scientific sense. Within SOMA it functions as the earliest admissible property through which anisotropic organization and directional configurational deformation produce a non-uniform admissibility structure, so that some directions become more favorable than others for persistence, transformation, or propagation. This arising is classified as a property because it expresses a directional condition of the admissibility landscape rather than an independent object or a separate process. In the Level-0 reconstruction it provides the first explicit bridge from directional support reconfiguration toward localized transport bias, field-level anisotropy, and later directional effective organization at higher levels.

arisings.Name: Localized Transport Bias
arisings.ShortDescription: Effect by which a localized configuration exhibits stable drift or asymmetric transfer feasibility within a directionally biased admissibility landscape.
arisings.Description: Localized Transport Bias denotes the effect by which a localized configuration exhibits stable drift or asymmetric transfer feasibility within a directionally biased admissibility landscape. It is not yet propulsion, external thrust, or completed physical transport law in the established scientific sense. Within SOMA it functions as the earliest admissible effect through which directional organization of support, directional configurational deformation, and a directional admissibility gradient become manifest as a persistent asymmetry in localization, displacement, or transfer feasibility. This arising is classified as an effect because it expresses an observable consequence of prior configurational and admissibility conditions rather than an independent object, carrier, or process. In the Level-0 reconstruction it provides the first explicit terminus of the directional branch and the last local precursor before possible higher-level formulations of effective field anisotropy and directional collective organization.

arisings.Name: Directional Configurational Deformation
arisings.ShortDescription: Process by which an already formed localized configuration deforms along a preferred orientation while retaining closure, redistributing its bounded support anisotropically.
arisings.Description: Directional Configurational Deformation denotes the process by which an already formed localized configuration changes its support distribution along a preferred orientation while retaining closure, bounded support, and integrable coherence. It is not yet arbitrary distortion, external force response, or a completed physical transport mechanism in the established scientific sense. Within SOMA it functions as the earliest admissible process through which an anisotropically organized configuration can reconfigure its support directionally without collapsing into loss of resonance, dispersion, or structural disintegration. This arising is classified as a process because it expresses an ongoing transformation of an already formed localized configuration rather than a static property or independent object. In the Level-0 reconstruction it provides the dynamic bridge from configurational anisotropy toward directional admissibility gradients and localized transport bias.

arisings.Name: Quantum Field Architecture
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level quantized field organization in which stable field sectors provide the admissible architecture for excitations, vacuum structure, and interaction channels.
arisings.Description: Quantum Field Architecture denotes the admissible pattern-level organization in which the effective first-level field becomes structured as a quantized field domain with stable symmetry sectors, excitation admissibility, vacuum organization, and interaction-channel architecture. At this level the field is no longer treated only as a coarse-grained carrier produced by Level 0 closure. It becomes a reproducible structural regime within which discrete excitations, gauge-related distinctions, vacuum-sensitive effects, and scale-dependent interaction forms can be consistently defined. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its primary ontological role is not one bounded object and not the full time-extended dynamics of propagation itself, but the stable architectural organization that makes such dynamics and excitations admissible. This arising establishes the structural basis for quarks, leptons, gauge-field excitations, vacuum fluctuations, and the later differentiation of strong and electroweak regimes at Level 1.

arisings.Name: Quarks
arisings.ShortDescription: Elementary object-level fermionic excitations carrying color charge and serving as the foundational carriers of hadronic structure.
arisings.Description: Quarks denote the admissible object-level excitations admitted within quantum field architecture that carry color charge and participate in non-Abelian gauge interactions. Within Level 1 they function as fermionic units characterized by spin-1/2, fractional electric charge, flavor identity, and transformation under SU(3) color symmetry. They are not free classical particles existing independently of field structure. They are identifiable quantum objects with definite flavor, charge and color quantum numbers, defined through quantized field excitations, gauge symmetry, and renormalizable interaction architecture. The heavier flavors decay through the charged weak current, and the top quark decays before it can hadronize. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an object because a quark is treated as a distinguishable carrier unit with definite quantum identity, even though isolated free realization is excluded by later confinement structure. This arising establishes the foundational object basis for strong-interaction matter and enables subsequent organization into hadrons, confinement regimes, and nucleonic structure.

arisings.Name: Leptons
arisings.ShortDescription: Elementary object-level fermionic excitations without color charge, serving as carriers of electroweak interaction structure; the electron is stable, while the muon and tau decay weakly.
arisings.Description: Leptons denote the admissible object-level excitations arising within quantum field architecture that do not carry color charge and therefore do not participate in strong interaction dynamics. Within Level 1 they function as fermionic units characterized by spin-1/2, flavor identity, electric charge or neutrality, and well-defined electroweak quantum numbers. They are not free classical particles detached from field ontology. They are identifiable quantum objects with definite electroweak quantum numbers, defined through quantized field excitations, electroweak gauge structure, and renormalizable interaction architecture. The electron shows no decay, whereas the muon, with a mean lifetime of about 2.2 microseconds, and the tau, with about 290 femtoseconds, decay through the charged weak current. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an object because a lepton is treated as a distinguishable carrier unit with definite quantum identity across interaction contexts. This arising establishes the complementary object basis to quarks within the quantum domain and enables weak processes, electromagnetic coupling, neutrino dynamics, and the later construction of atomic-scale organization.

arisings.Name: Gluons
arisings.ShortDescription: Object-level massless spin-1 color-octet gauge excitations of quantum chromodynamics that mediate the strong interaction and carry the color charge they couple to.
arisings.Description: Gluons denote the admissible object-level excitations of quantum field architecture associated with the SU(3) color gauge symmetry of quantum chromodynamics. Within Level 1 they function as massless spin-1 mediators of strong interaction structure in eight color states. Their defining feature is non-Abelian self-coupling, since gluons themselves carry color charge and therefore participate directly in the field dynamics they mediate. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an object because a gluon is a distinguishable carrier with definite spin and color quantum numbers, even though, like quarks, it is never realized in isolation. This arising establishes the carrier basis of strong-interaction dynamics and enables quark binding, running coupling behavior, confinement regimes, and later hadronic organization.

arisings.Name: Quantum Entanglement
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level nonseparable correlation structure in which multiple quantum excitations share a jointly defined state.
arisings.Description: Quantum Entanglement denotes the admissible pattern by which the states of multiple excitations admitted within quantum field architecture become jointly defined in a non-factorizable way. It is not a standalone object or a signal-transmission process. Instead, it is a reproducible structural correlation pattern embedded in quantum state architecture, such that the full configuration cannot be reduced to independent local descriptions of its components. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a relational organization that can recur across many physical realizations while remaining independent of any single carrier instance. This arising establishes the first explicitly nonlocal organizational motif at Level 1 and underlies quantum correlations, composite state structure, vacuum-linked coherence, and later quantum information phenomena.

arisings.Name: Vacuum Fluctuations
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level irreducible fluctuation structure of the quantum vacuum arising from field quantization and non-commuting observables.
arisings.Description: Vacuum Fluctuations denote the admissible pattern by which quantized field architecture retains irreducible fluctuation structure even in its lowest-energy vacuum regime. They are not classical noise and not stable standalone objects. Instead, they are recurrent structural patterns of transient vacuum activity arising from field quantization, operator non-commutativity, and the correlation structure of the quantum ground state. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a reproducible mode of vacuum organization that recurs across quantum field realizations without being reducible to any single localized carrier. This arising establishes the structurally active character of the quantum vacuum and underlies virtual processes, zero-point contributions, quantum corrections, and vacuum-sensitive interaction effects throughout Level 1.

arisings.Name: Asymptotic Freedom
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level scale dependence of non-Abelian strong interaction in which effective quark coupling weakens at high energies and short distances.
arisings.Description: Asymptotic Freedom denotes the admissible pattern by which the effective strong coupling in a non-Abelian gauge theory decreases as the characteristic energy scale increases or the interaction distance decreases. It is not a standalone object or a single dynamical event. Instead, it is a reproducible scale-dependent interaction pattern arising from renormalization-group flow in the presence of gluon self-interaction and quark degrees of freedom. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a general structural regularity of quantum chromodynamic behavior across scales rather than a bounded carrier or isolated process instance. This arising underlies the quasi-free behavior of quarks at high energies, enables perturbative QCD descriptions, and establishes the short-distance side of the strong-interaction regime transition that complements later confinement structure.

arisings.Name: Confinement
arisings.ShortDescription: Nonperturbative strong-interaction pattern in which color-charged excitations cannot persist as isolated free observable objects.
arisings.Description: Confinement denotes the admissible pattern by which color-charged excitations are restricted to color-neutral composite organization and cannot appear as isolated free observable objects. It is not a single object or localized event. Instead, it is a large-scale nonperturbative structural regularity of quantum chromodynamics in which the interaction energy associated with color separation grows with distance, so that free color is never realized: without dynamical quarks the static potential rises linearly, and with dynamical quarks the confining string breaks into a pair of color-singlet mesons at source separations of about 1.2 to 1.3 fm. The resulting restriction on admissible quark configurations enforces the color neutrality of all observable matter. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a reproducible regime-level organization of strong-interaction behavior across many carrier instances rather than a bounded carrier or standalone process. This arising defines the long-distance closure structure of QCD, complements asymptotic freedom at short distances, and establishes the admissible boundary condition for hadron formation, stable nuclear matter organization, and later atomic structure.

arisings.Name: Electroweak Symmetry Breaking
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level symmetry reorganization in which unified electroweak gauge structure is reduced, differentiating electromagnetic and weak interaction regimes.
arisings.Description: Electroweak Symmetry Breaking denotes the admissible pattern by which the unified electroweak gauge structure is reorganized into a lower-symmetry regime that differentiates electromagnetic and weak interactions. It is not a single particle, object, or isolated event. Instead, it is a structural pattern of symmetry reduction associated with the nonzero vacuum configuration of the Higgs field, through which gauge-field propagation modes and interaction properties become differentiated. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a reproducible organizational transformation of the quantum field architecture rather than a bounded carrier unit. This arising establishes the interaction asymmetry required for weak-boson mass, long-range electromagnetic behavior, chiral differentiation, and the later organization of particle stability, decay structure, and composite matter formation at Level 1.

arisings.Name: Higgs Mechanism
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level mass-generation mechanism in which quantum fields acquire effective mass through coupling to a scalar vacuum configuration.
arisings.Description: Higgs Mechanism denotes the admissible pattern by which gauge bosons and fermions acquire effective mass through coupling to a scalar field with a nonzero vacuum configuration. It is not a standalone particle or isolated event. Instead, it is a reproducible structural mechanism linking vacuum structure, field coupling, and symmetry topology so that originally massless field modes become differentiated into massive and massless sectors. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a general organizational rule of field behavior rather than a bounded carrier unit or a single process instance. This arising provides the specific mass-generation architecture associated with electroweak symmetry breaking and enables finite-range weak interaction, differentiated particle masses, and the stability conditions required for later composite matter formation at Level 1.

arisings.Name: Hadronization
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level composite organization in which quark-gluon dynamics produce color-neutral hadrons, most of them unstable resonances.
arisings.Description: Hadronization denotes the admissible pattern by which quark and gluon dynamics produce color-neutral composite states such as baryons and mesons, of which only the proton is stable as a free particle. It is not a single hadron object itself, but the structural formation pattern that governs how strong-interaction constituents pass from elementary excitation dynamics into color-neutral composite organization. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a reproducible organization regime of composite formation rather than a single bounded carrier or isolated process instance. This arising integrates quark object structure, gluon-mediated coupling, and scale-dependent strong-interaction behavior into a color-neutral formation regime that fixes the observable hadron spectrum and provides the structural basis for nucleonic matter, nuclear interaction, and later atomic organization.

arisings.Name: Protons and Neutrons
arisings.ShortDescription: Baryonic objects formed as color-neutral bound states with valence content uud and udd; the proton shows no decay, while the free neutron beta-decays and persists only when bound in nuclei.
arisings.Description: Protons and Neutrons denote the admissible object-level formation of baryonic composites with confined net three-quark (valence) content organized within the hadronic condensation regime. They are not generic hadronic patterns but bounded carriers with definite baryon number, mass and charge structure. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an object because protons and neutrons function as distinguishable units: the proton is stable on all observed time scales, with partial lifetime bounds above 10^34 years, while the free neutron decays with a mean lifetime of about 880 seconds and is stabilized inside nuclei. They serve as the foundational baryonic carriers for subsequent nuclear and atomic organization. This arising marks the consolidation of strong-interaction composite structure into the first long-lived matter objects that can support nuclei, isotopic diversity, and higher-level material formation.

arisings.Name: Particle Decays
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level transformation structure in which unstable quantum excitations convert into lighter or more stable configurations through allowed interaction channels.
arisings.Description: Particle Decays denote the admissible pattern by which unstable quantum excitations transform into lighter or more stable configurations under symmetry, conservation, and interaction-channel constraints. They are not arbitrary dissipations and not a single standalone process instance. Instead, they form a reproducible transformation pattern governing how unstable states redistribute into permitted products with characteristic lifetimes and branching structures. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a general organizational regularity of quantum transformation behavior across many specific decay events rather than a bounded carrier unit. This arising regulates matter stability, particle population flow, composite-state persistence, and quantum-level reconfiguration in both laboratory and cosmological settings.

arisings.Name: Vacuum-Structure Influence on Particle Properties
arisings.ShortDescription: System-level property by which structured quantum vacuum effects modify observable particle parameters and propagation behavior.
arisings.Description: Vacuum-Structure Influence on Particle Properties denotes the admissible property by which the structured quantum vacuum modifies the observable parameters and dynamical behavior of particle excitations. It does not describe an independent particle or a standalone vacuum pattern itself. Instead, it expresses a derived system-level property of the quantum domain in which vacuum polarization, virtual loop structure, and zero-point fluctuations alter effective mass, charge, coupling strength, and propagation relative to bare field definitions. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because it characterizes how particle observables depend on the surrounding vacuum organization rather than constituting a separate bounded object or generic correlation pattern. This arising formalizes the dependence of observable particle behavior on vacuum context and underlies renormalization, running couplings, and precision quantum corrections at Level 1.

arisings.Name: Elementary Particle Masses via Higgs Coupling
arisings.ShortDescription: System-level property by which coupling to the Higgs vacuum configuration generates masses for fundamental particles within the electroweak Standard Model framework.
arisings.Description: Elementary Particle Masses via Higgs Coupling denotes the admissible property by which fundamental particles acquire mass through coupling to the nonzero vacuum configuration of the Higgs field within the electroweak Standard Model framework. It does not describe all mass in nature and does not imply that the dominant mass of composite hadronic matter is generated directly by the Higgs field. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because it characterizes elementary particles through a derived vacuum-dependent attribute rather than constituting a separate bounded object or a generic symmetry-breaking pattern. This arising formalizes the Higgs-coupling basis of mass for elementary fermions and weak gauge bosons and establishes the mass hierarchy relevant for weak-interaction structure, decay channels, and particle kinematics at Level 1.

arisings.Name: Hadron Family Formation
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level taxonomic organization in which hadronic composites arrange into symmetry-related families with structured quantum-number relations.
arisings.Description: Hadron Family Formation denotes the admissible pattern by which hadronic composites organize into symmetry-related families such as baryon multiplets and meson multiplets. It is not a single hadron object or an isolated condensation event. Instead, it is a reproducible classification pattern emerging from quark content, confinement constraints, spin-flavor structure, and gluon-mediated binding relations. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a systematic organizational regularity across many hadronic carriers rather than a bounded object or standalone process instance. This arising establishes the taxonomic order of the hadronic spectrum, supports predictive relations among masses and transitions, and prepares the basis for identifying the nucleons as the lightest baryons.

arisings.Name: Neutrino Oscillations
arisings.ShortDescription: Process-level coherent flavor transformation in which propagating neutrinos change flavor through interference among distinct propagation eigenstates.
arisings.Description: Neutrino Oscillations denote the admissible process by which neutrino flavor states transform during propagation because produced and detected flavor states are coherent superpositions of distinct propagation eigenstates with nonzero mass splittings. They are not local interaction events occurring continuously along the path, but a propagation process of the leptonic sector defined by phase evolution over baseline and energy and by the flavor mixing structure. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because it cannot be described without the evolution of flavor amplitudes along the propagation path, while the mass splittings and mixing it depends on form a separate property. This arising establishes that neutrino flavor identity is not dynamically autonomous, constrains lepton-sector organization, and is essential for neutrino transport, astrophysical flux interpretation, and cosmological modeling at Level 1.

arisings.Name: Gluon Field Self-Organization
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level nonlinear organization in which gluon self-interactions generate structured nonperturbative QCD field behavior.
arisings.Description: Gluon Field Self-Organization denotes the admissible pattern by which gluon self-interactions generate structured collective field behavior in non-Abelian quantum chromodynamics. It is not a single gluon process or isolated carrier, but a reproducible organizational pattern emerging from the fact that gluons themselves carry color charge and therefore participate in closed feedback-rich interaction loops. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because it expresses a recurring structural regularity of strongly interacting gauge fields rather than a bounded object or standalone transformation event. This arising includes the formation of flux-tube structure, gluon condensate-like organization, and other nonperturbative field configurations that stabilize strong-interaction matter and provide the field-level basis for confinement, hadronic binding, and persistent QCD structure at Level 1.

arisings.Name: Quark Influence on Macroscale Matter Properties
arisings.ShortDescription: Cross-scale effect in which quark-level structure propagates through nucleonic organization to shape higher-level material properties.
arisings.Description: Quark Influence on Macroscale Matter Properties denotes the admissible effect by which quark-level parameters and strong-interaction structure propagate upward through hadronic and nucleonic organization to influence higher-level material properties. It is not the quark object itself and not a direct macroscale constituent. Instead, it is the produced cross-scale consequence of confined quark structure being inherited by protons, neutrons, nuclei, and eventually bulk matter. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an effect because it expresses an outward causal result of lower-level quantum organization that becomes operative in subsequent higher-level domains. This arising formalizes how quark masses, color interaction structure, and internal strong-dynamics constraints shape nucleon structure, nuclear binding behavior, matter density, compressibility, and the large-scale physical behavior of material systems.

arisings.Name: Quantum Fluctuations as Source of Primordial Cosmological Perturbations
arisings.ShortDescription: Cross-scale effect in which microscopic quantum field fluctuations seed primordial cosmological perturbations through early-universe amplification.
arisings.Description: Quantum Fluctuations as Source of Primordial Cosmological Perturbations denotes the admissible effect by which microscopic quantum field fluctuations become amplified by early-universe dynamics and produce persistent primordial perturbations that later shape large-scale cosmological structure. It is not the fluctuation pattern itself and not a cosmological object in isolation. Instead, it is the outward cross-scale consequence of quantum-level field variability being transferred into metric and density perturbations that later influence cosmic microwave background anisotropies and matter distribution. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an effect because it expresses a produced causal outcome of lower-level quantum organization that becomes operative in a higher-scale cosmological domain. This arising formalizes the widely used inflationary-cosmology picture in which quantum fluctuations seed primordial perturbations and thereby contribute to later large-scale structure formation.

arisings.Name: Effective Theories and RG Flow
arisings.ShortDescription: System-level property of scale-structured quantum description in which renormalization group flow maps high-energy field structure into low-energy effective behavior.
arisings.Description: Effective Theories and RG Flow denote the admissible property by which quantum field systems acquire scale-structured descriptions through renormalization group flow and effective reduction of high-energy degrees of freedom. This arising does not denote a single field object or isolated transformation event. Instead, it expresses a derived system-level property of quantum theory in which coupling parameters, operators, and interaction relevance evolve with scale so that low-energy behavior becomes describable by effective theories that retain only the structurally significant degrees of freedom. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because it characterizes the scale dependence and descriptive organization of field systems rather than constituting a bounded carrier or a recurring interaction motif alone. This arising formalizes scale separation, universality, and decoupling, and provides the conceptual basis for stable low-energy laws, running couplings, and effective field descriptions across physics.

arisings.Name: Virtual Excitations in Quantum Field Interactions
arisings.ShortDescription: Interaction-level property in which virtual excitations appear as internal contributions to observable quantum processes without existing as asymptotic free particles.
arisings.Description: Virtual Excitations in Quantum Field Interactions denote the admissible property by which perturbative quantum field descriptions include virtual excitations as internal contributions to observable interaction behavior without treating them as asymptotic free particle states. This arising does not describe independently existing particle objects, but an interaction-level structural feature of quantum field theory in which internal excitations contribute to propagation corrections, screening, antiscreening, polarization, and effective coupling behavior. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because it characterizes how interaction structure affects observable quantum processes rather than constituting a bounded carrier or a standalone vacuum pattern. This arising formalizes the role of virtual excitations in loop corrections, radiative effects, renormalized charges, and related vacuum-sensitive phenomena at Level 1.

arisings.Name: Photons
arisings.ShortDescription: Massless object-level gauge excitations of the electromagnetic field, serving as stable carriers of long-range electromagnetic interaction.
arisings.Description: Photons denote the admissible object-level excitations of the U(1) electromagnetic gauge field. Within Level 1 they function as massless, electrically neutral carrier units associated with electromagnetic propagation, radiative transfer, and interaction mediation. They are not classical waves detached from field ontology, but stable quantum objects identifiable as discrete excitations of the electromagnetic field. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an object because a photon can be treated as a distinguishable carrier unit with stable quantum identity across interaction and propagation contexts, even though its dynamics remain fully field-governed. This arising establishes the foundational electromagnetic mediator required for radiative transitions, long-range force transmission, atomic binding, and higher-level electromagnetic organization.

arisings.Name: W and Z Bosons
arisings.ShortDescription: Massive object-level gauge excitations of the weak sector, serving as carriers of short-range weak interaction after electroweak symmetry breaking.
arisings.Description: W and Z Bosons denote the admissible object-level excitations of the weak gauge sector that emerge as massive carriers after electroweak symmetry breaking and Higgs-based mass generation. Within Level 1 they function as distinguishable quantum mediator objects with definite masses, lifetimes, and interaction channels, enabling charged-current and neutral-current weak processes. They are not generic gauge patterns or massless field modes, but short-lived, identifiable resonances of the weak sector, with total widths of about 2.1 GeV for the W and 2.5 GeV for the Z, observed through their decay products. Within SOMA this arising is classified as an object because W and Z bosons are treated as bounded mediator excitations with definite mass, spin and charge across production and decay contexts. This arising establishes the short-range weak interaction carrier structure required for beta decay, neutrino scattering, flavor-changing weak processes, and the differentiation of weak dynamics from electromagnetic interaction.

arisings.Name: Nonzero Neutrino Mass and Flavor Mixing
arisings.ShortDescription: System-level property of the neutrino sector in which nonzero neutrino mass splittings and nontrivial flavor mixing make flavor states non-identical to propagation eigenstates.
arisings.Description: Nonzero Neutrino Mass and Flavor Mixing denotes the admissible property by which neutrinos possess nonzero mass splittings and a nontrivial mixing structure connecting flavor states to distinct propagation eigenstates. It does not specify the deeper mass-generation mechanism and does not assume that neutrino mass is produced by the same route as charged-fermion masses in the minimal Higgs description. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a property because it characterizes the neutrino sector through an experimentally established propagation-relevant structure rather than a bounded object or a generic formation pattern. This arising formalizes the fact that neutrino flavor identity is not identical to neutrino propagation identity and provides the structural basis required for oscillation phenomena, matter-enhanced flavor transformation, astrophysical neutrino interpretation, and cosmological neutrino modeling.

arisings.Name: Quantum Field Dynamics
arisings.ShortDescription: Process-level propagation, interaction, and state evolution of quantized fields within the stable architecture of Level-1 field organization.
arisings.Description: Quantum Field Dynamics denotes the admissible process-level evolution of quantized fields within the stable architecture of Level 1. It includes propagation of field modes, excitation updates, interaction-vertex realization, vacuum-sensitive dynamical response, and scale-dependent evolution under symmetry-constrained equations of motion. This arising is not the architectural existence of the field domain itself and not a bounded particle-like carrier. Instead, it is the ongoing dynamical regime through which the already constituted Quantum Field Architecture becomes operational as a time-extended interaction system. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a process because its identity depends on ordered evolution, coupling, and transformation through time rather than on static structural organization. This arising establishes the dynamical basis required for gauge-mediated interaction, virtual processes, vacuum fluctuation activity, decay channels, and the propagation behavior of excitations throughout Level 1.

arisings.Name: Vacuum Configuration
arisings.ShortDescription: Pattern-level organization of the quantum vacuum as a structured ground-state regime within quantum field architecture.
arisings.Description: Vacuum Configuration denotes the admissible pattern-level organization of the quantum vacuum as a structured ground-state regime within quantum field architecture. It is not a particle-like excitation, not a transient fluctuation, and not merely the absence of excitations. Instead, it is the stable background organization of field sectors in their lowest-energy admissible state, including symmetry-consistent ordering, ground-state constraints, and the structural conditions under which vacuum-sensitive effects can later arise. Within SOMA this arising is classified as a pattern because its primary ontological role is a reproducible structural regime of field organization rather than a bounded carrier or a time-extended propagating process. This arising establishes the vacuum-level background required for vacuum fluctuations, symmetry-sensitive mechanisms, virtual excitation structure, and later differentiated vacuum regimes such as electroweak vacuum organization.

arisings.Name: Higgs Vacuum Configuration
arisings.ShortDescription: Property-level nonzero scalar vacuum organization that defines the electroweak ground-state condition for later symmetry breaking and mass coupling.
